records.text: Dan Golthas is an apprentice leatherworker who recounts clawing out of the grave expecting a welcome from family. Instead, the family drove Dan from the village, screaming in a language Dan could no longer understand.

Deathguard Linnea monitors Scourge activity that slips past the Bulwark into Tirisfal, particularly near Balnir Farmstead. She stresses protecting the defenders' rear and supply lines, directs patrols and sends reports to Magistrate Sevren in Brill. She values effective patrol work and offers to commend it to her superior, Executor Zygand.

Deathguard Dillinger directs efforts against the Scourge near Brill and Agamand Mills, fearing a foothold for further attacks in Tirisfal. He expects courage from allies and relishes the destruction of hostile undead. After efforts to free the captive Ulag from the Lich King's influence fail, Dillinger regards killing him as the remaining way to release him.

Gunther Arcanus is a free-willed Forsaken necromancer and former Kirin Tor student, once friends with Bethor Iceshard and Thule Ravenclaw. Bethor's enchantment on his spellbook convinced him that Bethor too had escaped the Lich King's control. Still wary, Gunther demanded proof that a visitor opposed the Scourge; after learning of other free-willed undead, he agreed to join the Forsaken.

Bethor Iceshard is a Forsaken mage and former Kirin Tor student who knew Gunther Arcanus and Thule Ravenclaw before the Plague. Seeking useful necromantic knowledge for the Forsaken, he investigated Gunther, enchanted his spellbook to reveal that he too was free of the Lich King's control, and hoped to recruit him. Bethor also knows Thule's magic and prepared countermeasures against the former colleague's attacks.

Magistrate Sevren directs Forsaken investigations and defenses in Tirisfal. He seeks reports on Scourge crossing the border and uses Brill's death records to investigate a ring's owner. He also recruits proven agents for Bethor Iceshard's dangerous work against the Scourge, while admitting he does not know the mission's details.

Coleman Farthing once worked for the Agamands and stayed to defend their home when the Plague came; he blames their choice for condemning him and his family to undeath. He now seeks their remains and heirlooms, taking fierce satisfaction in their destruction. Though he knows it may be foolish, he hopes the Agamands felt fear before they lost even the last traces of their honor.

A mindless undead of the Scourge, counted among the fallen who overran the northern part of the Forsaken village. The Forsaken regard such former brothers and sisters as slaves of the Lich King and seek to destroy them.

A ghoul among the Scourge's mindless fallen overrunning the northern Forsaken village. The Forsaken describe these undead as former brothers and sisters enslaved by the Lich King and seek their destruction.
A young spider found around the mine northwest of the Forsaken village. Its presence contributes to the infestation that obstructs access to the mine's gold.
A spider infesting the gold mine northwest of the Forsaken village. The infestation obstructs the Forsaken's efforts to obtain gold from the mine.
A Scarlet Crusade fighter who treats opponents as tainted by the Scourge and calls for the Crusade to destroy them and smite evil in the region. Its combat cries express the order's militant cause.
A Scarlet Crusade fighter who treats opponents as tainted by the Scourge and calls for the Crusade to destroy them and smite evil in the region. Its combat cries express the order's militant cause.
A young scavenger of Tirisfal, this small creature belongs to the local wildlife rather than the town’s people.
A ragged scavenger found among Tirisfal’s wildlife.

Executor Zygand directs the Forsaken campaign against the Scarlet Crusade from Brill. He relies on intelligence gathered by Executor Arren and turns reports about Scarlet positions into targeted assignments, including strikes against commanders and their troops. He also oversees a town reward for Maggot Eye, a gnoll accused of stealing corpses for the Lich King’s army; the notice condemns the theft and declares mercy weakness.

Apothecary Johaan is a Royal Apothecary Society researcher in Brill, developing a plague intended to spread widely. He tests his concoction with gathered reagents, including murloc scales and spider venom, and says poisoning one victim is easy compared with plaguing a world. He also sends his findings to Apothecary Renferrel so the Society can pursue the New Plague for Sylvanas.

Deathguard Simmer addresses newcomers as fledgling Forsaken and urges them to prove themselves in service to the Dark Lady. He directs them to steal pumpkins from a nearby human farm and deliver them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.
A Rattlecage Soldier is a low-level soldier found in the Rattlecage area and nearby cemetery grounds.

Gretchen Dedmar is a Forsaken in Brill who once sewed body bags for soldiers in Sylvanas's army. The Plague of Undeath is advancing through her, and she fears the coming mindless state; she asks for pelts and thread to sew a blanket so she can keep serving the cause. She hopes Sylvanas will recognize those who fight for her.

A Bleeding Horror is one of the Scourge threats that slip behind the Bulwark’s defenses. Linnea’s patrol sends defenders east, especially to Balnir Farmstead, to kill these horrors before they threaten the rear or supply line.

A Rotting Ancestor is one of the Agamand dead raised through necromancy to strengthen the Scourge foothold at Agamand Mills. The assault on the Family Crypt targets these ancestors alongside Captain Dargol.
A Lost Soul is found in Tirisfal.

Wandering Spirits are among the Scourge threats that get past the Bulwark’s defenses. Linnea’s patrol sends defenders east, especially to Balnir Farmstead, to hunt them alongside Bleeding Horrors and protect the rear and supply line.
A Tormented Spirit appears in the Agamand area of Tirisfal.

A Wailing Ancestor is one of the Agamand dead raised through necromancy for the Scourge foothold at Agamand Mills. The assault on the Family Crypt targets these ancestors along with Rotting Ancestors and Captain Dargol; this one uses Wailing Dead in combat.
A Scarlet Crusade warrior in Tirisfal, this fighter condemns the Scourge's taint and vows to purge evil. In battle, the warrior relies on nimble reflexes.
A Scarlet Crusade missionary in Tirisfal, this fighter denounces the Scourge and invokes the Light's condemnation of evil. The missionary attacks intruders and casts a combat spell.
A Scarlet Crusade zealot in Tirisfal, this fighter denounces the Scourge's taint and vows to drive evil from the land. The zealot's battle cries reveal a crusading conviction.

A Scarlet Crusade friar in Tirisfal, this fighter condemns the Scourge and invokes the Light against evil. In battle, the friar uses healing spells, pairing religious conviction with support for the Crusade.

A Scarlet Neophyte of the Scarlet Crusade, who declares the Crusade’s campaign against those it calls tainted by the Scourge. The neophyte threatens its enemies and casts Frost Armor while out of combat.
A Scarlet Vanguard of the Scarlet Crusade, who declares the Crusade’s campaign against those it calls tainted by the Scourge. The vanguard threatens its enemies and uses a combat ability.
A Vile Fin Puddlejumper, found in several areas of the Eastern Kingdoms.
A Vile Fin Minor Oracle, found in several areas of the Eastern Kingdoms. In combat, it casts Lightning Bolt.
A Vile Fin Muckdweller, found in several areas of the Eastern Kingdoms.
A Decrepit Darkhound, found in several areas of the Eastern Kingdoms.
A darkhound encountered in the Eastern Kingdoms.
A darkhound encountered in the Eastern Kingdoms.
A duskbat found in the Eastern Kingdoms. It uses Ravage in combat.

Yvette Farthing is a Forsaken who once loved Thurman Agamand and urged him to leave Agamand Mills with her and her father. When his letter reaches her, she mourns him and suspects Brand meant him harm, then says love and her former life are behind her as she pursues new goals.
Mordo is the caretaker of the Deathknell crypt. He greets newly freed Forsaken waking there and directs them to Shadow Priest Sarvis at the chapel, who can explain their situation.

Sarvis explains that the Forsaken were freed from the Lich King's control by Sylvanas and now fight the Scourge and human holdouts. In Deathknell, he directs new Forsaken against the Mindless Ones and Rattlecage skeletons, whom he regards as former kin reduced to the Lich King's slaves. He also helps them prove themselves and understand their place among the Forsaken.

Executor Arren balances Deathknell's resource needs with the Scarlet Crusade threat. With little manpower, he sends help to clear spiders from the gold mine, then acts on scouts' reports of a Crusade camp. He calls the Crusade a danger to all undead and seeks intelligence on its agents and field commanders, forwarding recovered documents to his superior, Executor Zygand, so they can plan a decisive response.

Deathguard Burgess serves as a Brill guide, directing visitors to the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master. He also collects Scarlet Insignia Rings as proof of loyalty to Varimathras and the Dark Lady.
Gregor Agamand is identified as the father of Thurman Agamand, the eldest of his sons.
Nissa Agamand is one of the Agamands who fell to the Plague and became minions of the Scourge. Coleman Farthing asks for her remains.
Thurman is Gregor Agamand’s eldest son, described as tall and gentle. A letter written by him is addressed to Yvette Farthing.

Devlin is the sharp-tongued younger Agamand son, whose mad chattering is heard near the mills. He taunts his mother, father, and brother, says his family hates him, and insists that he is head of the family.
Captain Dargol leads the Scourge presence in the Agamand Family Crypt. This skeleton uses necromancy to raise Agamand ancestors for an attack on Brill.
A Scarlet Crusader assigned to guard Captain Melrache at the ruined tower in northern Tirisfal, this bodyguard is one of two targets in Brill’s mission against his raiding crew.

Novice Elreth tends the wounded, makes armor and clothing, and helps Shadow Priest Sarvis. She speaks as someone familiar with the risks facing new recruits and offers practical help. She calls Marla Fipps her friend and hopes Marla and Samuel may find peace together.

Captain Perrine is a Scarlet Crusade officer. Intelligence from Executor Arren, relayed by Executor Zygand, places his brigade at a ruined tower southwest of Brill and identifies him as a target in the Crusade campaign.

Captain Vachon commands Scarlet Crusaders described in Executor Arren's report as raiding from a ruined tower in southeastern Tirisfal near Balnir Farmstead. Executor Zygand presents Vachon as a significant target in the ongoing war against the Crusade.

Captain Melrache leads the Scarlet Crusaders reported to be raiding from a ruined tower in northern Tirisfal, beyond Faol's Rest. Executor Zygand calls him a ruthless commander and assigns a mission against him and his two bodyguards in the name of the Dark Lady.

Meven Korgal is a Scarlet Crusade agent sent from the Scarlet Monastery to Deathknell as a messenger. His shouted words call for the Crusade to fulfill its mission, cleanse the lands, and destroy the undead.
A Rot Hide gnoll whose combat cries show hunger for fresh meat and bones.
A Rot Hide mongrel whose combat cries hunger for fresh meat and bones. It is among the Rot Hides sent to gather corpses from Tirisfal’s mass graves.
A Night Web Matriarch is a beast found in Tirisfal Glades.
Deathguard Abraham serves as a Deathguard and offers city directions. Visitors can ask about the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master.
Deathguard Randolph is a humanoid Deathguard in Tirisfal Glades.
Deathguard Oliver is a humanoid Deathguard in Tirisfal Glades.
Deathguard Terrence helps people find their way around the city, directing them toward the bank, bat handler, inn, or stable master.
Deathguard Phillip is a humanoid Deathguard in Tirisfal Glades.

Deathguard Saltain organizes scavenging in Deathknell so newly risen Forsaken recruits can equip themselves. He expects recruits to search for useful discarded gear and speaks to them brusquely, but recognizes hard work with a better find. His words show the Forsaken's determination to provide for themselves.
Deathguard Bartrand is a humanoid Deathguard in Tirisfal Glades.
Deathguard Bartholomew offers city directions. It asks what visitors seek and lists the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master.
Deathguard Lawrence offers city directions. It asks what visitors seek and lists the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master.
Deathguard Mort offers city directions. It asks what visitors seek and lists the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master.
Deathguard Morris offers city directions. It asks what visitors seek and lists the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master.
Deathguard Cyrus offers city directions. It asks what visitors seek and lists the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master.

Maggot Eye is a gnoll outlaw described in Brill's wanted notice as stealing corpses for the Lich King's army. The notice says he was last seen near Garren's Haunt and condemns him for crimes against the Forsaken.

Rattlecage Skeletons are low-level undead encountered around Deathknell. Shadow Priest Sarvis describes them as mindless minions of the Lich King and treats thinning their numbers as a test for the Forsaken.
Muad is a named elite humanoid in Tirisfal Glades. He uses spells in combat and casts another spell when wounded.
Deeb is a named elite humanoid in Tirisfal Glades. He fights with Lightning Bolt and Shock, and tries to flee for help when badly hurt.
Stephen Bhartec is a named low-level undead found in Tirisfal Glades.
Daniel Ulfman is a named low-level undead found in Tirisfal Glades.
Karrel Grayves is a named low-level undead found in Tirisfal Glades.
Samuel Fipps was Marla Fipps's husband before the plague. He succumbed, became one of the mindless Scourge, and killed Marla; her last wish was burial beside her beloved Samuel.

A Scarlet Zealot held in the cellar of Gallow's End Tavern, he is desperately hungry when offered the laced pumpkin. His words swing from horror that he is rotting to pleas for food, the Light's protection, and the Scarlet Crusade.
A Tirisfal farmer, representing the region's everyday farm life and work.
A Tirisfal farmhand, part of the local workforce tending the region's farms.
Farmer Solliden stands out as a formidable Tirisfal farmer, more dangerous than the ordinary farm workers around him.
A Rot Hide gnoll scavenger that gathers the dead from Tirisfal's mass graves for the Scourge and snarls about fresh meat, showing a coarse predator's appetite.

Raleigh Andrean, once a chef, lives with a grief he describes as having gone cold. Deliah was his wife, and Valdred Moray was Raleigh’s good friend before murdering her. Recovering Deliah’s ring brings back Raleigh’s account of his numbness and the revenge that still drives him. After Valdred is killed, Raleigh keeps the murderer’s hands as a reminder of his friend’s betrayal.

Master Apothecary Faranell oversees the Royal Apothecary Society’s ambitious alchemical research and seeks help gathering substances for experiments aimed at producing a plague. The Society also values Apothecary Berard’s research after Arugal’s curse made him useless to it, and Faranell welcomes the recovery of Berard’s work for the Dark Lady’s cause. In the aftermath of the Wrathgate tragedy, he acknowledges the Society’s grave misguidance and seeks permission to continue its work in peace, while recognizing the distrust caused by Putress’s actions.
Archibald Kava is an Undercity merchant who sells cloth and leather armor and offers repairs. His shop serves travelers looking for practical equipment and upkeep.
Faruza is an herbalism trainer.
Joshua Kien is a general-supplies vendor who offers customers a chance to browse his goods.
Blacksmith Rand is an apprentice armorer who offers goods and repair services.
Harold Raims is an apprentice weaponsmith who offers goods and repair services.
Abigail Shiel is a trade-supplies vendor.

Dannal Stern trains warriors and teaches that their role includes protecting the Forsaken and their interests. He urges new Forsaken to serve Sylvanas, whom he credits with restoring their freedom despite the plague's continuing effects.

David Trias trains rogues in Deathknell and watches for promising prospects among the new faces. He says the Deathstalkers need capable agents, and that Lady Sylvanas sanctions their growing numbers; he warns recruits to keep their conduct clean and distinguishes trained agents from mere pickpockets. His advice and training point toward service as a disciplined blade in the Forsaken cause.

Dark Cleric Duesten trains Forsaken priests and frames their powers as tools for a people shaped by corruption and survival. He teaches that their faith rests in their own will, and warns a new priest not to rely on the Holy Light, ancestral spirits, or Nether creatures. In his view, the Forsaken's experience gives them lessons others can barely understand, and the weak and uninformed will one day look to them for aid and guidance.

Isabella trains Forsaken mages and urges them to return as they grow in power. She sees kinship in shared pain and suffering, and presents magic as a means to reclaim the Forsaken's land, lives, and destinies. Her warning is practical as well as ideological: magic still follows its rules, and its corrupting pull can become addictive, though discipline can resist it.

Maximillion trains Forsaken warlocks and treats freedom from control as a central cause. He argues that a slave remains a slave regardless of the master, even as warlocks seek power over creatures who serve them; he wants the Forsaken to choose their own allegiances and claims this fits Sylvanas's beliefs. He calls himself no traitor to the Dark Lady and offers to stand with those who share this struggle.

Rupert Boch is a warlock trainer who offers further instruction to those seeking warlock knowledge. His manner is imperious: he expects deference from students who approach him for training and dismisses those he considers unworthy of his time.

Cain Firesong trains undead mages and cautions them that untrained magic can burn its wielder. He directs mages toward Anastasia Hartwell for their first task and for reports of a magical disturbance in Undercity.

Dark Cleric Beryl teaches that the Forsaken draw on darkness while still needing the healing arts, and that both light and dark have their uses. She tests initiates by having them heal and fortify Deathguard Kel, then recognizes those who pass as having earned a place in her ranks. Beryl stresses the Forsaken’s history of corruption and decay and calls darkness their home.

Marion Call trains rogues and speaks of growing the Deathstalkers, whose blades serve Lady Sylvanas’s cause. She can direct a prospective recruit to Mennet Carkad, who has taken an interest in them; ignoring his summons has proved dangerous for others. Marion also offers an Elegant Letter through a gossip option.

Austil de Mon trains warriors and describes their role as protecting both their companions in battle and the interests of the Forsaken. He can refer someone willing to prove their value to the Dark Lady’s forces to Deathguard Dillinger in Brill.
Carolai Anise is an alchemy trainer in Brill. Her available interaction includes training and talent services.
Mrs. Winters runs a general-supplies shop in Brill, where customers can browse her goods.
Abe Winters is an apprentice armorer who offers armor for sale.
Oliver Dwor is an apprentice weaponsmith who offers weapons for sale.
Eliza Callen is a leather armor merchant who offers her goods for sale.
Deathguard Gavin helps visitors find the bank, bat handler, inn and stable master.
Deathguard Royann helps visitors find the bank, bat handler, inn and stable master.
The Captured Mountaineer is relieved to receive a drink, accepting anything to wet the whistle. The prisoner also insults the visitor and hopes to be rid of them.
Caretaker Caice is a caretaker.

Andrew Brownell is concerned by the Scourge’s alliance with the quilboar of Razorfen Downs. He directs the player to stop Amnennar the Coldbringer, whom he identifies as ruling the quilboar and linked to Ner’zhul, and asks for Amnennar’s skull as proof. Brownell frames the task as urgent, warning that the Scourge must not strengthen its ranks.
Thomas Arlento is an undead found in Tirisfal Glades.
Jamie Nore is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Doreen Beltis is an undead found in Tirisfal Glades.
Sahvan Bloodshadow is an undead found in Tirisfal Glades.
Maquell Ebonwood is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Randolph Montague is a banker.
Mortimer Montague is a banker.
Lexington Mortaim is a portal trainer who teaches mage portal magic. His dialogue treats the subject as demanding mental acuity and presents portal conjuration as a specialized mage talent.
A humanoid named Lucian Fenner.
A humanoid named Susan Tillinghast.

Keeper Bel'dugur is a guarded member of a secret order who recruits others to open chapters of it. He tests prospective members with three powerful relics before sharing Yagyin's Digest, and warns that the order must keep its signs discreet and remain careful, watchful, and patient. He also collects the work of Ur, a pre-Scourge Dalaran mage whose studies interest certain Forsaken. Bel'dugur values strength as necessary for Forsaken survival and reports service to the Dark Lady.

Hin Denburg is the Stranglethorn Vale zeppelin master, and he takes pride in his airship. He calls it the finest transportation money can build and mocks anyone who favors the Deeprun Tram or the gnomes behind it. His pitch is boastful and teasing as he urges travelers to ride to Grom'gol in style. He also announces when the zeppelin to Grom'gol has arrived.
Constance Brisboise is an apprentice clothier in the Undercity. She offers goods for sale, including through the merchant and supply options available to visitors.
Bowen Brisboise is a tailoring trainer in the Undercity. He greets visitors courteously and offers tailoring training.
Hamlin Atkins is a mushroom farmer who also offers food for sale. He is recorded as a creature, and the supplied evidence gives no spoken characterization.
Selina Weston supplies alchemy and herbalism goods. Her shop is a practical stop for anyone seeking materials for those trades.

Shelene Rhobart teaches leatherworking, and her greeting turns unexpectedly personal: she reflects on how little skin remains and how freeing that has become. Her matter-of-fact humor frames the trainer as someone facing bodily deterioration with a striking, unsentimental perspective.
Martine Tramblay is a fishing-supplies vendor. Her named shop role distinguishes her as a practical source of equipment for anglers.

Lordaeron Citizens are ordinary townsfolk rather than identified individuals. These citizens appears in several local areas, giving the settlement a population beyond its named merchants and trainers.
A Scarlet preserver and humanoid spellcaster.
A Scarlet Scout is an armed Scarlet-named combatant encountered in several local areas. It casts a spell when drawn into combat.
A Scarlet Crusade magician who fights with spells.
A Scarlet Crusade sentry who warns enemies that the Crusade will destroy those carrying the Scourge’s taint. He calls on the Crusade to smite the wicked and drive evil from the land.
A Scarlet Crusade augur who fights with spells.
A Scarlet Crusade disciple who fights with spells.

Genavie Callow says the plague took her family and left her estate looted and burned. She blames Kenata and the Dabyrie family for stealing her remaining valuables, then demands revenge against Kenata and her children. Her gratitude for their deaths is brief: she says she can turn to more lucrative pursuits.

Parqual Fintallas is an undead historian in the Undercity who values knowledge over strength. He tests students on the Scourge’s origins and the lore behind the undead threat, using questions that distinguish what they have learned. His distrust of the Scarlet Crusade reflects its campaign against the undead, and he regards its members as enemies of the Forsaken.
William Montague is a banker in the Undercity. He provides access to banking services for visitors who want to manage their stored belongings.
Ophelia Montague is a banker in the Undercity. She provides access to banking services for visitors who want to manage their stored belongings.

Michael Garrett is the bat handler in the Undercity. He arranges bat travel, including routes to places a rider has already visited and whose bat master they have met; the Sepulcher is one such destination. He describes long-distance travel as a good use for a bat.

Eunice Burch teaches cooking in the Undercity. She treats cooking as a lifelong pursuit and recognizes a shared interest in it. For advanced instruction, she points aspiring cooks toward Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan, whom she regards as a master of the culinary arts.
Ronald Burch is identified as a cooking-supplies merchant in the Undercity. His role is to provide cooking supplies; the available evidence does not establish further personal details.
Tawny Grisette is identified as a mushroom vendor in the Undercity. Her role is to sell mushrooms; the available evidence does not establish further personal details.
Eleanor Rusk is identified as a general-goods merchant in the Undercity. Her role is to provide general goods; the available evidence does not establish further personal details.

Gordon Wendham is the Undercity's weapons merchant, serving customers with a reserved, service-minded manner. When the Sepulcher's order reaches him, he accepts it as an honor to serve those who serve the Dark Lady. He keeps his weapons clean and ready for use.
Louis Warren is a weapons merchant, offering goods for customers to browse. His specific trade is weapons, distinguishing his shop role from the armor merchants nearby in the same district.

Lauren Newcomb is a light armor merchant, offering goods for customers to browse. Her specialty is light armor, setting her trade apart from the weapons and heavy armor merchants in the same district.
Timothy Weldon is a heavy armor merchant, offering goods for customers to browse. His trade is heavy armor, a specialty he shares with Walter Ellingson in the same district.
Walter Ellingson is a heavy armor merchant, offering goods for customers to browse. His trade is heavy armor, a specialty he shares with Timothy Weldon in the same district.
Daniel Bartlett supplies trade goods and lets customers browse his offerings. His shop is distinct from the nearby weapons and armor merchants, whose stock serves more specialized equipment needs.
Thomas Mordan is a reagent seller, with a goods-browsing interaction for customers. His role centers on practical supplies for spellwork.

Kaal Soulreaper is a warlock trainer who directs students to Menara Voidrender in Ratchet for further instruction. His training dialogue judges a student's will and readiness, giving his counsel an exacting tone.
Luther Pickman trains warlocks, whose requests for further training address him as “my master.”
Richard Kerwin trains warlocks, whose requests for further training address him as “my master.”
Kaelystia Hatebringer identifies herself as an undead mage trainer and warns that magic can burn the untrained. Her counsel ties magical study to caution.
Pierce Shackleton is a mage trainer whose greeting identifies him as an undead mage and advises travelers that magic burns the untrained. His counsel emphasizes caution in magical study.

Anastasia Hartwell is a Forsaken mage whose work includes studying how far the Plaguelands' taint has spread into Tirisfal. She also investigates a magical disturbance in the Undercity, seeking to learn whether it arose by chance or from an attack so the mages can prepare for future threats. Her duties include training mages and directing investigations.
Charles Seaton is a blade merchant whose wares are available to browse.
Sydney Upton is a staff merchant whose wares are available to browse.
Morley Bates is a fungus vendor whose wares are available to browse.
Silas Zimmer is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.

Armand Cromwell is a fishing trainer in the Trade District of Stormwind. He can point skilled anglers toward Old Man Heming in Booty Bay for “The Bass and You,” and tells those who have advanced beyond his skill to seek Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh.
Lizbeth Cromwell is a merchant selling fishing supplies.
Hannah Akeley is a reagent merchant.

Josef Gregorian teaches tailoring and fashions spellfire robes at the Magic Quarter’s tailor shop. Expecting customers referred by Anastasia, Josef checks their linen and mana gems, praises the cloth, but admits he cannot judge the gems’ magical quality. Josef stitches the robe and announces when it is finished. Josef states a preference for working with human skin rather than cloth.
Millie Gregorian is a merchant selling tailoring supplies.
Josephine Lister is a master shadoweave tailor and trainer. Josephine describes shadow as lying between light and dark, and warns that its powers extend beyond what the listener has yet seen.
Lucille Castleton is a robe vendor in the Undercity, offering clothing for customers browsing her goods. Her role is distinct from the city's book and poison suppliers.
Salazar Bloch deals in books in the Undercity. His book trade sets him apart from the city's robe and poison suppliers.

Carolyn Ward trains rogues in the Undercity. Her trainer's dialogue speaks of the Deathstalkers growing under Lady Sylvanas's sanction, while a separate training response directs someone to their class trainer. The available evidence does not establish how those conditional lines apply to individual visitors.

Miles Dexter is an Undercity rogue trainer. Trainer dialogue speaks of the Deathstalkers growing under Lady Sylvanas's sanction. In the request attributed to him, he sends the recipient to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt at Ravenholdt Manor, saying the matter is secret and giving no further details.

Gregory Charles trains rogues in the Undercity. His trainer's dialogue speaks of the Deathstalkers growing under Lady Sylvanas's sanction; another conditional response redirects someone to their class trainer. The supplied evidence does not establish when either response applies.
Ezekiel Graves supplies poisons in the Undercity, serving a specialist trade distinct from the city's robe and book vendors.

Graham Van Talen introduces aspiring engineers to the choice between goblin and gnome specialization. He favors goblin engineering, praising its explosives and gear, while dismissing gnome devices as unreliable. He directs students to the specialists who handle each discipline, and warns that choosing one makes membership permanent. He also regards knowledge as a weapon in the Dark Lady’s war.
Elizabeth Van Talen sells engineering supplies and invites visitors to browse her goods.

Once a librarian, Arthur Moore died amid wars and plagues and was later restored to his own mind. He resents what was done to him, but now intends to fight rather than surrender. He trains leatherworkers.
Joseph Moore supplies leatherworking goods. His shop role makes him a practical contact for leatherworkers seeking materials and equipment.
Jonathan Chambers supplies bags. His shop role makes him a practical contact for people looking for carrying gear.
Mary Edras teaches First Aid. She points advanced practitioners toward Doctor Gregory Victor, whom she identifies as the authority able to improve their skill, at Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands.
Nathaniel Steenwick is a merchant specializing in thrown weapons. Visitors can browse his goods.
Christoph Walker trains warriors. He describes their role as protecting companions in battle and defending the Forsaken's interests, giving his instruction an allegiance-focused outlook.

Angela Curthas trains warriors and speaks with blunt impatience, telling visitors not to waste her time. Her training dialogue also frames a warrior's duty as protecting companions and the Forsaken's interests.
Baltus Fowler trains warriors. His training dialogue describes the warrior's role as protecting companions in battle and defending the Forsaken's interests.
James Van Brunt teaches blacksmithing with grim enthusiasm: he speaks of forging blades to gut foes and hammers to crush skulls, and welcomes the prospect of bloodshed.
Samuel Van Brunt deals in blacksmithing supplies. His listed services include browsing goods and repairing equipment, giving smiths a source for materials and upkeep.
Brom Killian teaches mining. He offers instruction directly, making him a practical guide for those learning to draw ore from the earth.
Sarah Killian deals in mining supplies, serving miners who need goods for their work. Her listed services include browsing goods.
Geoffrey Hartwell is a weapon merchant. His listed services include browsing goods and repairing equipment, covering both arms and their upkeep.
Francis Eliot is a weapon merchant. His listed services include browsing goods and repairing equipment, covering both arms and their upkeep.
Benijah Fenner is a weapon merchant, identified by his named trade and the goods-browsing interaction associated with his merchant role.
Nicholas Atwood is a gun merchant. His named trade sets him apart among the local merchants, and his native record includes a goods-browsing interaction.
Abigail Sawyer is a bow merchant. Her named trade distinguishes her role among the local merchants; the native record supports browsing goods.
Basil Frye is an apprentice blacksmith with an ambitious vision: he hopes one day to forge weapons and armor from the bones of his enemies.
Aelthalyste is a priest trainer whose greeting invokes Elune. She offers instruction in priestly ways and information about dual talent specialization.
Father Lankester is a priest trainer. His recorded dialogue addresses Elune, and his training options concern priestly instruction, talent unlearning and dual talent specialization.
Father Lazarus presents himself as an insignificant servant and offers priest training.
Doctor Marsh relies on Algernon to supply his alchemy work, so he can avoid gathering herbs; he says he would be glad never to see nature again.
Algernon sells alchemy supplies and invites visitors to browse the goods.
Doctor Herbert Halsey trains alchemy while working with colleagues to test deadly substances on their enemies; he aims to brew plagues on an unprecedented scale.
Boyle is an undead found in Tirisfal Glades.
Christopher Drakul is the Guild Master at the Undercity Guild Registry, where visitors can ask about forming a guild or creating its crest.
Martha Alliestar trains aspiring herbalists. Her straightforward invitation—“I can instruct you in herbalism”—keeps the exchange focused on learning the craft.
Katrina Alliestar sells herbalism supplies.
Lavinia Crowe teaches enchanting. In her greeting she notes that she gets few visitors and asks whether a visitor seeks something specific, giving her welcome a reserved, practical tone.
Thaddeus Webb sells enchanting supplies. His place in Brill’s trade is practical: enchanters can browse his goods for materials used in their craft.

Zachariah Post is an undead horse merchant speaking for the Royal Apothecary Society. He presents the Forsaken steeds as having endured trials and emerged stronger than mortal flesh, and invites customers to inspect them. His patience is limited: he says the Society shares that impatience and ties his willingness to discuss his steeds to exalted standing with Undercity.

Velma Warnam teaches Skeletal Horse Riding. She presents the lesson as paid training and says she requires exalted standing with the Forsaken of Undercity to teach a riding skill. A pamphlet sent from her advertises riding training and mount purchases; its return quest names her as the recipient, while the training exchange identifies her role directly.
Felicia Doan sells trade supplies.
Edward Remington designs guild tabards and helps guilds create their crests.
Merill Pleasance is a tabard vendor. Customers can ask about lost tabards, including the Blood Knight Tabard and the Tabard of the Hand.

Apothecary Zinge conducts research for the Royal Apothecary Society, eager to experiment with new toxins. She considers herself clever enough to turn Keever's work into a successful project and rewards assistants who remain useful without wasting her time. She modifies a sampling kit for desert fieldwork and coordinates with Vivian Lagrave over an ancient text thought to benefit their research.

Patrick Garrett is a bat-pen sweeper in Undercity who sees the job as an insult to his family standing. He hopes to reclaim a family weapon left in Uldaman and treats it as his birthright, offering silver for help. Once reunited with it, he boasts to the bats and celebrates the Garrett heirloom.
Tyler is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Edward is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Robert Gossom applauds, cheers and shouts.
Richard Van Brunt applauds, cheers and shouts.
Marla Fowler is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Chloe Curthas is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Andrew Hartwell is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Riley Walker is a humanoid resident whose idle routine includes occasional out-of-combat emotes.

Brother Malach oversees the staged training of Edward and Tyler, calling them to successive challenges and praising their progress. He directs Lysta to summon captives and undead for the trials; after dismissing one test as no challenge, he promises a harder final fight. His instructions show a demanding instructor focused on testing the young warriors' mettle.

Sergeant Houser drills fighters with caustic insults and demands that they keep striking until ordered to stop. Houser treats the sword as an extension of its wielder and warns that practice targets may show mercy, but the Lich King will not. Poor effort draws ridicule rather than reassurance.
Travist Bosk is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Eldin Partridge is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Alyssa Blaye is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Venya Marthand is the named recipient of rattlecage skulls gathered for a novice warlock's lesson in binding a servant.
Mattie Alred is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Helena Atwood is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Edrick Killian is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
The Practice Target is a target for practice, providing a focus for training.

Carendin Halgar teaches warlocks to summon voidwalkers and succubi. He warns students that summoned beings can overwhelm the unwary, and cautions them against succubi’s charms. Egalin taught Carendin to command a voidwalker; Carendin recalls that his own overconfidence nearly cost him control. He holds students to high expectations and stresses care in wielding their power.
Lysta Bancroft is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.

Innkeeper Renee runs an inn in Brill, where guests can rest and browse her goods. Her welcome is warm enough, but her letter response is a performance of sweetness that turns sharply sarcastic: she jokes about hearing from her mother in Deathknell, then tells the visitor to get lost and spend coin instead of loafing. Beneath the bite, she offers help to anyone who needs it.

Clyde Kellen is a fishing trainer in Tirisfal Glades. His available training interaction identifies him as a trainer, while his title specifies fishing; the supplied evidence gives no further personal details.

Godrick Farsan assists Carendin Halgar with the succubus summoning plan, identifying two men whose hearts will serve as bait. He recounts Dalin Forgewright’s flight from the plague and care for refugees, and Comar Villard’s lasting search for his kidnapped wife. Godrick calls the men fools, showing contempt for the goodness and devotion that make them useful to the plan.
Vance Undergloom teaches enchanting, inviting travelers to explore the mysteries of the arcane.

Gerard Abernathy boasts of new domination techniques involving torture, magic and invasive surgery on a conscious woman. Gerard speaks possessively of a pet and a new toy, seeking others' reactions to the work. Gerard also orders Theresa to carry something to Father Lankester.
Theresa is Gerard's mindslave, addressing Abernathy as lord and obeying commands. Theresa carries messages or items between Abernathy and Father Lankester, speaking deferentially on their behalf.

Joanna Whitehall praises Gerard's experimental achievements despite having doubted his abilities, and wants to inspect his failed experiments. Joanna treats his female pet as something to house-train, breed or fit with a bell collar. Joanna also sells goods, but can dismiss unwanted customers brusquely.

Leona Tharpe disapproves of Gerard's experiments while finding their results impressive. Leona asks how Gerard achieved lasting domination of a woman who still retains awareness, knowledge, speech and the ability to perform tasks. This curiosity concerns the method; Leona does not claim to know how it works.

Samantha Shackleton is an arcane researcher who works through books on magic, including “Magic and the Ways of Power” and Maginor Dumas’s “Magical Flows and How They Effect the World.” She tracks down specific passages, questions her theories when the evidence disagrees, and knows she needs a better system for filing her books.
Selina Pickman is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.

Jezelle Pruitt teaches warlock summoning, explaining how different demons help: a felhunter is useful against spellcasters, while a felsteed aids travel. Her lesson guides students through the imp, voidwalker, and felhunter before moving to the felsteed, and she invites them to stay for another class.
Winifred Kerwin is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Adrian Bartlett is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Victor Bartholomew is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Davitt Hickson is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Reginald Grimsford is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Ageron Kargal directs aspiring warlocks to Carendin Halgar for further training in the Undercity’s Magic Quarter.
Deathguard Lundmark is an Undercity guard who helps visitors find city services, including the bank, bat handler, inn, and stable master.
Apothecary Vallia is named as an apothecary of the Royal Apothecary Society.
Apothecary Katrina belongs to the Royal Apothecary Society. She is reported to have bought a bottle of perfume from Norman, the innkeeper, providing a lead in an investigation of its supplier.
Apothecary Lycanus works with the Royal Apothecary Society.

Apothecary Keever experiments with serums for the Royal Apothecary Society, forcing fluid down a weary man's throat and testing another liquid on a toad. Keever suspects excess earthroot when a result disappoints and tries a second serum. Speaking of Keever in the third person, the apothecary complains that Abernathy keeps taking the subjects needed for this work.
This captive is a human woman held in a cage.
This captive is a human man held in a cage.
This captive is a male dwarf held in a cage.
Cedric Stumpel is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Hepzibah Sedgewick is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Kayla Smithe is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.
Gina Lang is a humanoid found in Tirisfal Glades.

Martha Strain is associated with a referral for warlocks seeking to bind a dreadsteed: the quest directs them to Mor'zul Bloodbringer near the Altar of Storms. Its text describes the undertaking as perilous and suited to a warlock of considerable mastery.
Zane Bradford is a wand vendor who offers goods and repairs.
Nurse Neela is a First Aid trainer who teaches medical techniques. For advanced instruction, she directs trainees to Doctor Gregory Victor at Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands.
Mirelle Tremayne runs a heavy armor shop in the Undercity. She sells armor and can repair equipment.
Gillian Moore runs a leather armor shop in the Undercity. She sells armor and can repair equipment.
Sheldon Von Croy runs a cloth armor shop in the Undercity. He sells armor and can repair equipment.
Rand Rhobart is a skinning trainer. His services also include instruction in other skills, unlearning talents and pet skills, and access to dual talent specialization.

Jorah Annison works as a cartographer in the Undercity, but cares far more for books than maps. He has deep knowledge of ancient texts and pursues the scattered parts of the Tome of the Cabal, an old warlock work on summoning a felhunter. He studies the recovered tome and hopes to read more rare works, including books about necromancy and the Dark Lady. He treats even wild rumors as possible paths to truth.
Sergeant Rutger is a sergeant found in Tirisfal Glades.

Velora Nitely was a renowned Lordaeron armorsmith before her death and still makes brutal legguards in Undercity. She commissions sturdy Dragonmaw shinbones and judges whether they will hold up in her work. Undeath has dulled her interest in smithing, though she prefers it to becoming a mindless Scourge minion. Her jokes about lost senses keep faltering; she admits she cannot tell whether they are funny.

Mennet Carkad recruits and tests prospective Deathstalkers in Undercity’s Rogues’ Quarter, then assigns covert work on Lord Varimathras’ orders. His missions include investigating threats to the Forsaken and pursuing leads around Andron. He speaks with measured confidence, expects recruits to prove themselves, and stresses discretion: the work may be fatal, and knowing less can be safer. He also judges their progress and can advance their training in the shadow arts.
A Rift Spawn can become angered and attack. It can be drawn into a coffer or escape into the void.

Andron Gant is a contact for the Deathstalkers, keeping a ledger of information for their employers and expecting them to decide whether to continue their arrangement. He also handles a separate exchange involving a note for Jediga. His slurred greetings and payment suggest a heavy drinker; he remains guarded about what his associates tell their messengers.

Estelle Gendry outfits the Deathstalkers with thieves’ tools. Mennet sends new initiates to her before missions, and her shop offers both an initial set and replacements. She is part of the organization’s practical support for its growing ranks under Lady Sylvanas.

Innkeeper Norman tends an inn in the Undercity, where he offers lodging and goods. During Hallow's End, he makes a mint a playful reward for chicken clucking and answers the seasonal greeting in kind. He also sells perfume and cologne, though he sees little of the fuss about them.

Calvin Montague approaches Deathknell visitors with a letter errand, describing Brill's inn as a comfortable stop and promising pay. The arrangement is a deception: when confronted about the letter and money, he denies owing anything and turns the dispute into a fight. After losing, he admits he lied about the payment and hands over less coin than promised.
Ratslin Maime is a named individual found in Tirisfal Glades.
Killian Hagey is a skinning trainer. His trainer services include training.
Gothard Winslow is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
A cockroach, a small critter of the Undercity.

Alessandro Luca runs Blue Moon Odds & Ends and offers a testing kit to the Royal Apothecary Society. His polished greeting and playful complaint that Apothecary Zinge never visits give his shopkeeper manner a flirtatious edge.

Oran Snakewrithe is a Witherbark scholar who studies troll writings and serves the Dark Lady. She welcomes the chance to examine Rin'ji's tablet, carefully puts it away, and expects her discovery to please the Dark Lady. She also directs the destruction of Highvale records to cut the high elves' lines of communication.

An elite Deathguard of the Forsaken, a heavily armed humanoid guard associated with Undercity. This level-75 veteran has no recorded gossip or service flag, so the supplied evidence supports a martial guard role rather than a spoken personality or personal history.

Chemist Cuely investigates the illness Thersa Windsong brought back from Azshara, testing water she drank at the Ruins of Eldarath. He sees her worsening condition as a chance to study the plague and argues she should help find a cure for the Forsaken, even if the work may cost her life. His elixir takes hold quickly; he then turns to the remaining samples, hoping they can aid Lady Sylvanas and the Forsaken.

Tauren adventurer Thersa Windsong came to Undercity seeking help for a sickness that is tearing her up inside. She has already consulted priests and shamans without success, and the city makes her feel unwelcome. With no time to seek another remedy, she accepts Chemist Cuely’s elixir despite finding his eagerness disturbing, and hopes the Earthmother will watch over her spirit.

Jeremiah Payson is undead and once bore the Felstone name. When confronted with news from his dead sister Janice, he bristles at being treated like a vulture, then asks about her package. He sells cockroaches and ruefully jokes that he cries when one is stepped on.
Auctioneer Leeka provides auction services.
Auctioneer Epitwee provides auction services.

Zapetta announces zeppelin arrivals and departures on the Durotar route. Her brother proposed the trade venture, but she ended up living on this side; she asks travelers returning from Orgrimmar to bring her fresh meat, weary of food that died weeks before it stopped moving.
Anya Maulray is a stable master who can stable pets and help recover lost companions.
Morganus is a stable master who can stable pets and help recover lost companions.

Chemist Fuely studies slimes and oozes in the Apothecarium. Following Lady Sylvanas's order to investigate Azeroth's natural phenomena, he compares corrupted Felwood samples with apparently untainted Un'Goro slimes. He suspects the creatures share a basic makeup but are changed by their environment, and sees the samples as grounds for further research.
Bayne is a rare humanoid combatant.
Ressan the Needler is a rare beast combatant.
Fellicent's Shade is a rare undead creature named for Fellicent. It casts spells in combat.
Sri'skulk is a beast.

Junior Apothecary Holland welcomes returning as a Forsaken member of the Apothecary Society, considering it a fitting fate. He impatiently demands doom weed, scorning the abomination collecting gloom weed and refusing to explain the error again. He greedily accepts the correct reagent, first calling it a service to himself before crediting the Lady.

Gordo is an undead collector who enjoys picking flowers and compares it to killing. Large hands make gathering difficult, so Gordo asks others to bring gloom weed to Master Holland, who actually wants doom weed. Gordo is puzzled by Simmer's insults and reports Johaan's advice to have a tailor fix Gordo's stomach.

Royal Overseer Bauhaus is an Undercity census officer who accesses the city’s population records through arcane methods and sharpened mental discipline. Visitors ask him where people are or whether they are dead; he sounds practiced at the repetition and treats identifying Jeremiah Payson with dry humor about his cockroach trade.

High Executor Derrington commands Horde operations from the Bulwark in the Western Plaguelands. He welcomes capable heroes to the dangerous frontier and directs the campaign against the Scourge in Andorhal. His plans include marking the city’s watchtowers for a later assault and exploiting the Scarlet Crusade’s presence to divert its attention. He praises precise execution and frames service there as duty to the Horde.

Officer Garush is a proud member of the Argent Dawn, which he describes as a force against evil rather than a political body. He welcomes both Horde and Alliance as allies in that cause. He oversees the Dawn's commission and exchanges Scourgestones for valor tokens.

Hasana identifies herself as one of the Argent Dawn's authorized equipment and materiel quartermasters. She explains that Officer Garush awards valor tokens for service under the Dawn's commission, and that greater standing brings access to more items. Her assignments concern the Dawn's magic-resistant mantles, including a chromatic mantle reserved for its mightiest heroes.

Harbinger Balthazad serves the Horde as a herald, greeting visitors and offering news from both continents and beyond. He is a point of contact for regional calls to action, directing interested Horde members to the leaders named in those announcements.

Alexi Barov is a proud, contemptuous heir of House Barov and one of its last two surviving heirs. He resents his brother Weldon for fleeing the war and remaining human, and seeks to secure the family fortune for himself. If the deeds to the family lands are recovered, Alexi turns to hiring an assassin to remove Weldon, treating the murder as a matter of inheritance and addressing hired help with open disdain.
Franklin Lloyd is an engineering trainer. He presents himself as a professional and has little patience for idle gossip.

Doctor Martin Felben is an apprentice alchemist whose past as a human shapes his view of the Forsaken's conflict with the living. He says that knowing human weaknesses from experience gives the Forsaken an advantage, revealing a practical and calculating perspective on his former people.
Victor Ward is an apprentice tailor at the Bulwark. He notes that visitors are uncommon and offers them goods, reflecting the outpost's remote, visitor-facing trade.
Rhiannon Davis is an apprentice tailor at the Bulwark. She says tailoring can be useful and recalls once sewing her own arm back on, giving her trade talk a strikingly personal, grimly comic note.

Shadow Priestess Vandis coordinates the Bulwark's effort to subvert the Western Plaguelands cauldrons and turn their plague against the Scourge. She directs missions to secure toxin samples and tracks reports from the field, while Apothecary Dithers analyzes samples and advises on reagents. Vandis expects the sabotage to be ongoing and believes sustained efforts could weaken the Scourge.

Apothecary Dithers is an apothecary at the Bulwark whose work spans two Plaguelands problems: preparing solutions for the cauldrons and studying Scholomance to develop a Skeleton Key. He treats the key as a practical project, explaining its materials and using a solvent to fit Araj’s scarab into it. His remarks are impressed with capable helpers, while his cauldron instructions are pragmatic about costly, unstable supplies.
Malcomb Wynn is an apprentice enchanter in the Western Plaguelands. He brushes off idle visitors and demands they state their business, giving him a brusque, guarded manner.
The Green Skeletal Warhorse is an undead horse with a skeletal form and green coloration.
An Argent Dawn defender whose identity is defined by service to the order and its defensive role.

Bardu Sharpeye is preparing to enter the Plaguelands from his camp at the Bulwark. He is pursuing a rumor about a human wizard in Hearthglen who crafted a remarkable bow or gun for the Scarlet Crusade before they killed him. Bardu sees the story as evidence that the Crusade’s mistrust of arcane magic has grown.

Mickey Levine’s family worked at Northridge Lumber Mill for the Dumah family, and the mill where he spent his childhood is now held by the Scarlet Crusade along with Hearthglen. He is committed to driving the Crusade out and wants to cripple its use of the lumber mill by releasing Plagueland termites there. His anger is personal as well as political: he remembers his family losing both their livelihoods and their lives, and resents the Crusade’s claim to holiness.
Theodore Griffs is a named person who greets visitors with “Hello.”

Archibald is a Weapon Master who trains visitors in the use of weapons and points them toward other weapon masters for instruction beyond his own. He is brisk and impatient with visitors, asking them to make it fast because he is very busy.
Claire Willower welcomes visitors to Brill who bring a Collector’s Edition gift voucher. She offers a choice of unique companion gifts in exchange, greeting the visitor warmly.
A blue skeletal horse.
A brown skeletal horse.
A red skeletal horse.

Deathguard Kel is a wounded guard who has protected Brill from gnolls. After a priest heals and fortifies him, he says he can take on the gnolls with the priest’s power behind him, thanks the priest, and wishes them shadow’s protection.
Werg Thickblade sells leatherworking supplies.
Lieutenant Sanders is a lieutenant in Tirisfal Glades.
Nardstrum Copperpinch is a Smokywood Pastures vendor in Tirisfal, offering goods to visitors.
Jaycrue Copperpinch is a Smokywood Pastures vendor in Tirisfal, offering goods to visitors.
The Purple Skeletal Warhorse is an undead horse, a skeletal mount rather than a person with a separate character identity.

Ralston Farnsley is the Horde cloth quartermaster, rallying donations to replenish Forsaken cloth and bandage supplies. His appeal is blunt: the drive pays no money, runecloth is urgently scarce, and continuing aid will earn recognition for the Undercity.
A Wickerman Guardian is an elite creature associated with a seasonal world event. When drawn into combat, it casts Strike.

Darkcaller Yanka is a Forsaken celebrant who turns Hallow's End into a weapon against Southshore. She urges visitors to spoil the town's ale and celebrates the trouble this causes, framing the mischief as a tribute to Forsaken liberation from Scourge enslavement. She pairs her gleeful hostility toward the Alliance with the festival's treats and practical errands.

Elder Darkcore is one of the elders honored during the Lunar Festival. The elder welcomes homage to the olden races and offers a token. The elder's festival words speak of the new year, the bright moon and the awakening of the ancients; the exchange also names other elders visitors may ask about.

Elder Graveborn is one of the elders honored during the Lunar Festival. The elder welcomes homage to the olden races and offers a token. The elder's festival words speak of the new year, the bright moon and the awakening of the ancients; the exchange also names other elders visitors may ask about.
Auctioneer Stockton is identified by name as an auctioneer.
Auctioneer Yarly is identified by name as an auctioneer.
Cain is an auctioneer.
Naxxremis is an auctioneer.
Tricket is an auctioneer.
Rhyker is an auctioneer.

Senior Sergeant Grimsford recruits help for the Horde's preparations for the Ahn'Qiraj War. Grimsford says the collectors cannot meet their material goals without outside assistance and directs volunteers to Warlord Gorchuk, the organizer in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits.
Officer Gothena handles Undercity commendations, recording deeds and exchanging signets. Gothena praises the sacrifices behind those signets and encourages adventurers to continue their service.

A Cenarion Circle herald carries the Lunar Festival’s invitation to Azeroth’s peoples. In the capital cities, the herald points visitors toward the local moonlit celebration and can explain the festival; the invitation is broad, but the arrangements are made city by city.

An Undercity reveler greets the Lunar Festival with warmth and a wry sense of its chill, joking about numb fingers while lighting fireworks. The reveler also explains the moonbeam’s route and warns that old factional grudges still limit travel to enemy cities, even during the celebration.
A Steamwheedle bruiser is a formidable goblin enforcer associated with the Steamwheedle name.

Fenstad Argyle is concerned about tainted fragrances and urgently wants to identify their supplier. His suspicions lead Zinge to assess possible mind-control ingredients. He looks to Apothecary Katrina's account of buying perfume from Innkeeper Norman as a lead in the search.

Mara Rennick is a merchant who supplies Innkeeper Norman with perfume and cologne bought from Apothecary Staffron Lerent. She describes Lerent as odd and distances herself from possible wrongdoing by him. Willing to point an investigator toward her supplier, she argues that an innocent man has nothing to hide.
A scout of the Argent Dawn.
An Argent Dawn messenger who warns of Scourge attacks across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms and urges both Horde and Alliance to take up arms to defend their lands.
An Argent Dawn initiate who provides a Lesser Mark of the Dawn through a magical-item request.
An Argent Dawn cleric who provides a Mark of the Dawn through a magical-item request.
An Argent Dawn priest who provides a Greater Mark of the Dawn through a magical-item request.

Lieutenant Rukag serves the Argent Dawn and urges defenders to investigate the Scourge outside the Undercity while reducing their numbers. Rukag considers the glowing runic circles significant and interprets reported voices as evidence of communication, recoiling at the minds that might be contacted. A recovered crystal prompts suspicion that the Scourge intended to create a necropolis base camp inside the city, and a call for continued vigilance.

The Festival Talespinner is a festival historian who keeps its past and documents the current year's celebrations. He says festival fires hold power and suspects sacred flames burn in enemy cities. He invites tales of the stolen city flames and responds to their return with interest.

Mehlar Dawnblade is a bitter, vengeful elf who blames Uther Lightbringer for mishandling Arthas's training and, in turn, for Quel'Thalas's destruction. He seeks revenge on Uther and demands the defilement of his tomb; when the attempt fails and Uther's forgiveness is reported, Mehlar rejects it and insists Uther was at fault.

This Forsaken commoner takes part in seasonal festival chatter in Tirisfal. During the Lunar Festival, the commoner urges fellow Forsaken to seek their elders and consider their wisdom; at Midsummer, the conversation turns to summer celebrations, fireworks and festival shopping. Their remarks connect ordinary social life with the seasonal gatherings.

Rex Pixem is the named Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit arena battlemaster. His arena dialogue is brisk and unsparing: he tells an unsuitable challenger to stop wasting his time, while inviting a would-be competitor to prove they belong in the arena battlegrounds. He presents entry to the circuit as something a fighter must earn.

Derek the Undying presents himself as an undead mage trainer and gives travelers a pointed warning: magic will burn the untrained. He addresses a fellow mage with a teacher's practical caution, treating the study of magic as something that calls for care.

The Tirisfal Pink Elekk is a seasonal event target presented as one of the pink-elekk hallucinations troubling drinkers. The apparitions are visible while drunk or wearing Synthebrew Goggles, and players are sent to zap elekks at beer gardens, including this one.

This apprentice serves as a Voodoo Brew vendor for T'chali's brewery. The greeting is relaxed and colloquial, pitching the brew as the best in the realms. The same named vendor appears at several festival locations, tying the role to the traveling celebration.

Kraxx is a zeppelin engineer who complains that the stench where he works merits hazard pay. He compares conditions with his brother Krixx in Orgrimmar, then points travelers to his zeppelin tracker for the Orgrimmar and Grom'gol routes.

The Traveling Orphan is a child whose lines mourn a dead mother or father and imagine that parent putting out fires. Another line asks what is happening, giving the character a confused, vulnerable response amid the danger.

The Masked Orphan Matron's dialogue centers on protecting Horde children from the Headless Horseman's fires and honoring those who keep them safe. She urges the children to emulate brave heroes and fight for the Horde, and bluntly hopes they will grow strong enough to die in glorious battle; that prospect, she says, brings tears to her eyes.
An apprentice of Drohn's Distillery and its brew vendor, this character confidently claims that no one in Azeroth can match the quality of the brew.

The Tirisfal Glades Flame Keeper welcomes visitors to honor the local festival flame and the fires of other Horde settlements. The keeper dismisses Alliance fires as unworthy and urges their desecration.

A Master Flame Eater teaches visitors new ways to handle fire at the Fire Festival in Horde capitals. The flame eater welcomes celebrants, urges them to honor the local flame and warns them not to get burned.
A Midsummer merchant offering festival goods for visitors to browse.
A hunter instructor.
Meefi Farthrottle is the Howling Fjord Zeppelin Master. Meefi directs travelers aboard the Cloudkisser to Vengeance Landing and announces its arrival for boarding, describing the vessel as majestic.
Elder Edward Cairn invites visitors to whisper a secret code from the Worldwide Invitational event, offering Tyrael’s Hilt in return.
Walter Soref is a locksmith who offers help with lost keys. Visitors can ask about missing keys to Scholomance, the Arcatraz, the Shattered Halls and Searing Gorge.
Margaux Parchley teaches inscription.
Ickabod Pimlen sells inscription supplies.
An Alliance siege vehicle, identified as battlefield equipment.

Vol’jin supports the Horde’s effort to retake the Undercity. He briefs arriving fighters on Putress’s apothecaries and Varimathras’s demons, warning that blight is being used against Horde troops. He urges champions to assist Thrall and Sylvanas and directs those ready for the assault to the Warchief.
Horde Demolishers are mechanical siege units aligned with the Horde. This one hurls boulders while out of combat.

Warsong Battleguards are Horde guards in the Battle for Undercity. Their shouts voice loyalty to the Horde and anger at Putress, whom one calls a wretch and says will not escape; another threatens to burn an unnamed target rather than hand it over.

Sylvanas Windrunner, the Banshee Queen, is personally invested in the defense of her city: she grieves over what has been done to it and vows swift, merciless vengeance on the traitors responsible. During the Battle for Undercity she guides the Warchief toward the Royal Quarter, warns of a trapped shaft, and detects demonic magic, while expecting danger from Varimathras and Putress.

Broll Bearmantle serves as an Alliance contact during the Undercity operation. He expects heroes sent by Varian and challenges an arrival who does not seem to fit that expectation, giving his greeting a wary, testing edge.
Valeera Sanguinar is a humanoid in Tirisfal Glades.
Stormwind Elites are elite Alliance soldiers serving Stormwind.
Alliance Flying Machines are mechanical flying units serving the Alliance.

King Varian Wrynn rallies Alliance forces in the assault on the Undercity, demanding justice for the Wrathgate dead and condemning Putress. He calls on Jaina’s strength but speaks with deep hostility toward Thrall and the Horde. He recalls being thrown into orc arenas, linking those experiences to his personal anger. He knows the orc battle cry “Lok’tar ogar” means “victory or death.”

This portrayal identifies Lady Jaina Proudmoore as ruler of Theramore. She initially answers a royal command promptly, but the corpses and overwhelming stench she encounters disturb her. Jaina urgently pleads with Varian to stop and refuses to help him continue, expressing regret that events did not have to unfold this way.

Warchief Thrall rallies the Horde to reclaim Undercity, honoring fallen comrades and calling for unity against injustice. Yet he fears that the hopes of his parents and Doomhammer have been lost, and longs for an absent old friend’s counsel. In his response after the assault, he sees renewed Alliance–Horde conflict as a battle with no victor, but insists the march toward Icecrown must continue and places hope in the heroes on whom the world’s future depends.

A Spring Gatherer researches the magic of Noblegarden eggs. Unable to get an explanation from the druids, the gatherer asks egg hunters for shell fragments while allowing them to keep the contents. Grateful for a sample, the gatherer cautions that more may be needed for conclusive results.

A Noblegarden merchant who welcomes visitors to the celebration and invites them to join the fun. The merchant is associated with the Egg Basket and Noblegarden Chocolate exchange, helping make the egg hunt part of the festivities.

William Saldean runs the Grain & Feed shop and offers training. He was visiting relatives when Lordaeron fell and believes he will never return to Westfall. He wonders whether his family survived, and says he more often wonders why he no longer cares.
A black skeletal horse, its frame a stark reminder of death.

A cheerful Forsaken spirit reunited with friends and family, sharing old stories. After enjoying all the food they prepared, the spirit asks for more Bread of the Dead and expresses gratitude with a small holiday gift.
A hostess at Pilgrim’s Bounty welcomes visitors to the feast and invites them to try every dish at a Bountiful Table. She can also explain how the tables work.

Miles Standish helps visitors learn Pilgrim's Bounty cooking in the Undercity courtyard. His seasonal work also includes keeping the feast supplied: he sends word when stuffing and chutney run low, and thanks those who bring more. He turns to others to keep the serving dishes stocked.
Rose Standish is the Pilgrim's Bounty vendor in Tirisfal Glades. Visitors can browse her goods.

Roberta Carter trains cooks at the Pilgrim's Bounty gathering in Undercity. She expects more students during the feast and also worries about how quickly the cranberry chutney disappears, joking that the abominations may be eating it. She asks visitors to help prepare another batch.

William Mullins helps keep Undercity's Pilgrim's Bounty tables supplied, though he finds the work strange when they no longer need to eat. He has promised the hostess to watch the tables, so he asks for help with candied sweet potatoes after Roberta Carter recruits him to prepare them. Even so, he insists that tradition matters.
An ochre skeletal warhorse, identified by its distinctive ochre name and skeletal form.
The ghostly Forsaken celebrants greet visitors with thoughts of reunion: they are glad to visit with friends and family again, celebrating and sharing stories of old.
A Pilgrim's Bounty supply barrel stocked for visitors to browse as a vendor.

Magistrix Erembria handles the Wintergrasp battle queue. She greets visitors and explains the current battle situation: one exchange says the Horde holds Wintergrasp Fortress and invites players to speak with her when battle is about to begin; another says battle has begun and urges support for the Horde forces. Her guidance follows the changing battle state.

A Kor'kron overseer, this orc watches the Forsaken and apothecaries in the halls, mistrusting both after the Wrath Gate. He warns visitors against suspicious behavior and abominations, insisting the Forsaken must answer to the Horde's watch.

Overseer Kraggosh is a suspicious, forceful guard over the apothecaries at the pit. He says their work cannot proceed without his permission, distrusts them because of Putress's actions at the Wrath Gate, and keeps Faranell under watch.
Dark Ranger Clea can cast Hooked Net in combat.
Dark Ranger Anya can cast Hooked Net in combat.
Dark Ranger Cyndia can cast Hooked Net in combat.
Timothy Cunningham is a bat handler who greets travelers with “Going somewhere?” and calls for guards.

Kwee Q. Peddlefeet is a Crown Chemical Co. event mascot who promotes the Charitable Charms program. He explains that mascots distribute Lovely Charm Collector’s Kits and suggests making bracelets for friends, loved ones, or faction leaders to show appreciation.
A junior investigator in the inquiry into the Crown Chemical Company. Steamwheedle seeks help with the investigation and points interested helpers to Detective Snap Snagglebolt in Orgrimmar.

place_records.text: You are in Tirisfal Glades, Horde land in the Eastern Kingdoms. Its main settlements are Brill, Deathknell, the Ruins of Lordaeron and the Bulwark, all held by the Horde, and the Bulwark guards the border with the Plaguelands. Scourge slip past its defenders now and then, Scarlet Crusade patrols press in from the north, and darkhounds roam the countryside.

You are in The Bulwark, a Horde outpost on the edge of the Western Plaguelands. High Executor Derrington commands the Horde's operations here and directs the campaign against the Scourge in Andorhal, while Shadow Priestess Vandis works to subvert the Plaguelands cauldrons and turn their plague against the Scourge. Argent Dawn officers and quartermasters, who welcome both Horde and Alliance as allies, are posted here too.

You are in the Ruins of Lordaeron, where the Undercity of the Forsaken stands. In its Magic Quarter Anastasia Hartwell studies how far the Plaguelands' taint has spread into Tirisfal, and she investigates a magical disturbance in the city. Mennet Carkad is in the Rogues' Quarter, and Lord Varimathras is in the Hall of the Dark Lady.

You are in Deathknell, a Forsaken village in Tirisfal Glades. Shadow Priest Sarvis directs new Forsaken against the Mindless Ones, which have overrun the north side of the village, and Executor Arren watches the Scarlet Crusade, which he calls a danger to all undead. Deathguard Saltain sends the newly risen to search the stacked boxes for gear.
You are in Night Web's Hollow, a spider-infested stretch around a gold mine northwest of the Forsaken village. The Night Web spiders there keep the Forsaken from getting the mine's gold.
You are in Solliden Farmstead, a farm in Tirisfal Glades. Scarlet Warriors and hostile farmhands threaten it, and Farmer Solliden himself is among the dangers.

You are in Agamand Mills, a place near Brill that Deathguard Dillinger fears the Scourge will use as a foothold for attacks into Tirisfal. Darkeye Bonecasters, Cracked Skull Soldiers and Rattlecage Soldiers are its main dangers, along with rotting and wailing ancestors.

You are in Brill, a Horde town in Tirisfal Glades. Executor Zygand directs the Forsaken campaign against the Scarlet Crusade from here, and Magistrate Sevren wants reports on Scourge crossing the border. Gnolls roam the area north of Brill's graveyard, near the mass gravesite, and rotting dead wander the outskirts.
You are in Whispering Gardens, in Tirisfal Glades. Scarlet Crusade magicians, scouts, sentries, augurs and disciples are the dangers here.
You are in Terrace of Repose, in Tirisfal Glades. Scarlet Magicians, scouts and preservers are the dangers here, along with sentries, augurs and disciples.
You are in Brightwater Lake, in Tirisfal Glades, where Clyde Kellen teaches fishing. Cursed darkhounds, vampiric duskbats and shambling horrors haunt the lake.

You are in Gunther's Retreat, an island that is home to Gunther Arcanus, a free-willed Forsaken necromancer. Hungering dead and shambling horrors roam it, and Gunther is wary of strangers until they prove they oppose the Scourge. A Scourge agent, Lillith Nefara, uses an altar off the island's southern coast.
You are in Garren's Haunt, in Tirisfal Glades. Rot Hide gnolls and mongrels roam it, and Rot Hide graverobbers and a maggot eye are among its dangers.

You are in Balnir Farmstead, a farmstead in Tirisfal Glades. Bleeding horrors and wandering spirits haunt its fields, and vampiric duskbats and cursed darkhounds range through it. Fellicent's Shade still walks here.

You are in Cold Hearth Manor, a Horde settlement in Tirisfal Glades. Constance Brisboise, an apprentice clothier, sells goods here, and Bowen Brisboise teaches tailoring. Rotting dead and ravaged corpses still shamble through its grounds.
You are in Crusader Outpost in Tirisfal Glades. Scarlet zealots and friars, cursed darkhounds and vampiric duskbats trouble the outpost, and Captain Vachon is the most notable of its enemies.

You are in The North Coast, a stretch of shore in Tirisfal Glades. Vile fin muckdwellers, minor oracles and puddlejumpers crowd its shore, while cursed darkhounds and vampiric duskbats roam the sand. Deeb is a hostile figure here.

You are in Whispering Shore, a shore in Tirisfal Glades. Vile fin oracles, muckdwellers and puddlejumpers haunt it, along with decrepit darkhounds, and sand sharks swim its waters. Muad is a hostile figure here.
You are in Faol's Rest, a place in Tirisfal Glades where a spirit healer offers a return to the living, presented as a choice.
You are in Scarlet Watch Post, a post in Tirisfal Glades. Scarlet vanguards and neophytes stand watch, with scarlet friars and bodyguards, and cursed darkhounds and vampiric duskbats prowl around it.
You are in Stillwater Pond, a pond in Tirisfal Glades. Ravaged corpses and rotting dead wander its banks, and cursed and decrepit darkhounds hunt there.
You are in Nightmare Vale, a vale in Tirisfal Glades. Cursed and decrepit darkhounds, vampiric duskbats and scarlet missionaries roam it, and Ressan the Needler is a hostile figure here.

You are in Venomweb Vale, a vale in Tirisfal Glades. Vicious night web spiders and ravenous darkhounds fill it, with vampiric duskbats, scarlet zealots and friars among its dangers. Lieutenant Sanders serves here as a lieutenant.
